chunks: And from him (Al-Hadith) from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn Ayyar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

From a man, a Mu'addar (one who has not yet performed the obligatory Hajj), who died and had not performed the Hajj of Islam, and he had wealth. He said: 'A Mu'addar who has no wealth should perform Hajj on his behalf.'

key_terms.حَجَّةَ الْإِسْلَامِ: The first obligatory Hajj performed in one's lifetime
key_terms.صَرُورَة: A person who has not yet performed the obligatory Hajj
key_terms.يَحُجُّ عَنْهُ: He performs Hajj on his behalf

ai.seo_question: Who performs Hajj for a deceased person who left wealth but never performed their own obligatory Hajj?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the financial and spiritual mechanics of *Hajj al-Badal*, specifying that a *Mu'addar* (one who has not yet performed their own obligatory Hajj) may act as the proxy using the deceased's estate. It highlights the Shia juristic consensus that the obligation of Hajj is transferred to the heir's wealth, allowing a financially dependent believer to fulfill the duty on behalf of the deceased, thereby ensuring the continuity of religious obligations beyond death.
